reason: The C^1-regularity conclusion is not justified by the validated inputs. They provide only C^1 graph charts g_U, so their derivatives Dg are merely continuous; the tangent bundle has only C^0 transition functions/local frames unless C^2 chart regularity or C^1 dependence of the tangent spaces is separately proved. Thus the sentence asserting an everywhere-invertible C^1 matrix B(U) silently assumes precisely the missing regularity. The general inference used is false: for the C^1 graph M={(x,|x|^(3/2))}, projection of tangent vectors to their first component is the restriction of an ambient smooth fibrewise isomorphism TM -> M x R, but its fibrewise inverse sends (x,a) to (a,(3/2)sgn(x)|x|^(1/2)a), which is not C^1 at x=0 for a nonzero. Finite-dimensional matrix inversion cannot repair this because the matrix is only continuous in a C^1 graph frame. A C^2 graph theorem, joint C^1 control of Dg_U(0), or a separate C^1 tangent-frame construction is required.
